targetTexts.1: My brothers, as you hold out your faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ, do not show favoritism.
targetTexts.2: Suppose a man comes into your meeting wearing a gold ring and fine clothes, and a poor man in shabby clothes also comes in.
targetTexts.3: If you lavish attention on the man in fine clothes and say, “Here is a seat of honor,” but say to the poor man, “You must stand” or “Sit at my feet,”
targetTexts.4: have you not discriminated among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?
targetTexts.5: Listen, my beloved brothers: Has not God chosen the poor of this world to be rich in faith and to inherit the kingdom He promised those who love Him?
targetTexts.6: But you have dishonored the poor. Is it not the rich who oppress you and drag you into court?
targetTexts.7: Are they not the ones who blaspheme the noble name by which you have been called?
targetTexts.8: If you really fulfill the royal law stated in Scripture, “Love your neighbor as yourself,” you are doing well.
targetTexts.9: But if you show favoritism, you sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors.
targetTexts.10: Whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles at just one point is guilty of breaking all of it.
targetTexts.11: For He who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not murder.” If you do not commit adultery, but do commit murder, you have become a lawbreaker.
targetTexts.12: Speak and act as those who are going to be judged by the law that gives freedom.
targetTexts.13: For judgment without mercy will be shown to anyone who has not been merciful. Mercy triumphs over judgment.
targetTexts.14: What good is it, my brothers, if someone claims to have faith, but has no deeds? Can such faith save him?
targetTexts.15: Suppose a brother or sister is without clothes and daily food.
targetTexts.16: If one of you tells him, “Go in peace; stay warm and well fed,” but does not provide for his physical needs, what good is that?
targetTexts.17: So too, faith by itself, if it does not result in action, is dead.
targetTexts.18: But someone will say, “You have faith and I have deeds.” Show me your faith without deeds, and I will show you my faith by my deeds.
targetTexts.19: You believe that God is one. Good for you! Even the demons believe that—and shudder.
targetTexts.20: O foolish man, do you want evidence that faith without deeds is worthless?
targetTexts.21: Was not our father Abraham justified by what he did when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?
targetTexts.22: You see that his faith was working with his actions, and his faith was perfected by what he did.
targetTexts.23: And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness,” and he was called a friend of God.
targetTexts.24: As you can see, a man is justified by his deeds and not by faith alone.
targetTexts.25: In the same way, was not even Rahab the prostitute justified by her actions when she welcomed the spies and sent them off on another route?
targetTexts.26: As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without deeds is dead.
